problems.q: How many years are in a century?
Fill in the blank: A millennium is a period of ______ years.
True or False: The dates 'BC' (or BCE) count backward toward the year zero.
Which happened first, 500 BC or 500 AD? Explain why.
problems.answer: 500 BC happened first, because BC dates come before AD dates (BC counts backward before year zero and AD counts forward after it).

problems.q: What is the main reason historians use timelines?
problems.answer: To put events in order from oldest to newest.

problems.q: What is a primary source?
problems.answer: A source that comes straight from the time being studied, such as a diary, clay tablet, or old coin.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: A textbook or a museum sign written later by someone who studied the past is called a ______ source.
True or False: An old coin made during the time being studied is a primary source.
Give one example of a primary source and one example of a secondary source.
problems.answer: Primary example: a diary, clay tablet, or old coin. Secondary example: a textbook or a museum sign.

problems.q: Why do historians consider primary sources to give the most direct evidence about the past?
problems.answer: Because primary sources come straight from the time being studied, rather than being made later by someone who only studied the clues.

problems.q: What is historical inquiry?
problems.answer: Asking questions about the past and hunting for evidence to answer them, almost like a detective.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Historians look at who made a source and ______ they made it.
True or False: Two people can describe the same event in different ways.
Name two other subjects that history connects to.
problems.answer: Any two of: geography, economics, and government.

problems.q: Why is it important for historians to compare different sources instead of trusting just one?
problems.answer: Because different sources can describe the same event differently, so comparing them helps find what really happened and spot bias.

problems.q: Which way do latitude lines run, and what do they measure?
problems.answer: Latitude lines run east-west and measure how far north or south you are.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Longitude lines run north-south and measure how far ______ or west you are.
True or False: The exact location of a place is found where a latitude line and a longitude line cross.
What map tool shows you which way is north, south, east, and west?
Explain how latitude and longitude lines work together to find an exact spot on Earth.
problems.answer: Latitude tells how far north or south a place is and longitude tells how far east or west; where the two lines cross gives the exact location.

2-2.title: Types of Maps and Map Projections

problems.q: What does a political map show?
Fill in the blank: A ______ map shows landforms like mountains and rivers.
True or False: Because Earth is round and maps are flat, every map projection stretches or shrinks parts of the world a little.
What kind of map would you use to show climate or population?
Why does every flat map distort some part of the Earth?
problems.answer: Because Earth is round (a sphere) and a map is flat, so turning the round surface into a flat one stretches or shrinks parts of the world.

2-3.title: Rivers, Seas, and Where People Settle

problems.q: Name two things rivers provided that helped early people survive.
problems.answer: Fresh water for drinking and water for farming.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Seas became ______ for trade and travel.
True or False: Many of the world's first civilizations grew beside rivers and along coastlines.
Why did early people often settle next to rivers?
problems.answer: Because rivers gave fresh water for drinking and farming, which they needed to survive and grow food.

problems.q: How did living near the sea help ancient people?
problems.answer: The sea acted as a highway, making trade and travel to other places easier.

problems.q: What is cultural diffusion?
problems.answer: The spreading of ideas, goods, religions, and inventions from one group of people to another.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Cultural diffusion happened through trade, travel, migration, and even ______.
True or False: Only goods, never ideas or religions, can spread through cultural diffusion.
Give one example of something that spread from one ancient civilization to another.
problems.answer: Any one of: the alphabet, new foods, or beliefs/religions.

problems.q: Explain how trade could lead to cultural diffusion.
problems.answer: When people from different groups trade goods, they also meet and share ideas, inventions, and beliefs, which spreads culture between them.

problems.q: How did hunter-gatherers get their food?
problems.answer: They moved around to hunt animals and gather wild plants.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: About ______ years ago, some groups learned to plant crops and raise animals.
True or False: Farming let people stay in one place instead of always moving.
Name one thing farming allowed people to do that hunting and gathering did not.
problems.answer: Any one of: store food, build permanent homes, or grow into larger communities.

problems.q: Why did learning to farm change the way people lived?
problems.answer: Farming let people stay in one place, store extra food, build permanent homes, and grow into larger communities instead of moving to hunt and gather.

3-2.title: Farming, Metal Tools, and the Rise of Civilization

problems.q: What happened when farming produced extra food?
problems.answer: Not everyone had to grow crops, so people could become builders, priests, traders, or leaders.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Learning to work metals like ______ gave people stronger tools and weapons.
True or False: Extra food meant everyone still had to farm and no one could take other jobs.
Name two new jobs people could take once not everyone had to farm.
problems.answer: Any two of: builders, priests, traders, or leaders.

problems.q: Explain how having extra food helped lead to the first civilizations.
problems.answer: Extra food freed some people from farming so they could specialize in other jobs, which led to bigger populations, towns, and eventually the first civilizations.

problems.q: Name three features that most civilizations have.
problems.answer: Any three of: cities, organized government, a writing system, specialized jobs, social classes, and a shared religion or culture.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: A civilization usually has a ______ system so people can record information.
True or False: A civilization is just any big group of people, with no special features.
Where did the earliest civilizations with all these features develop?
Why do these characteristics help us tell a civilization apart from a small village?
problems.answer: Because a small village usually lacks features like cities, organized government, writing, specialized jobs, and social classes, while a true civilization has all of them.

problems.q: On which continents do archaeologists find the oldest evidence of humans?
Fill in the blank: By following bones, tools, and cave ______, scientists can map the routes early humans took.
True or False: Early human migrations spread people to nearly every continent.
Name two kinds of evidence scientists use to trace early human migration.
problems.answer: Any two of: bones, tools, and cave art.

problems.q: Why is studying old bones and tools useful for understanding human migration?
problems.answer: Because their locations and ages let scientists trace the routes early humans took as they slowly spread across the planet.

problems.q: What does the word 'Mesopotamia' mean?
Fill in the blank: Mesopotamia sat between the Tigris and ______ Rivers.
True or False: The rich farmland of Mesopotamia was nicknamed the Fertile Crescent.
Why was the soil in Mesopotamia so good for farming?
problems.answer: Because the rivers flooded and left behind rich soil.

problems.q: Explain how the rivers helped a civilization grow in Mesopotamia.
problems.answer: The Tigris and Euphrates flooded and left rich soil, making the land great for farming, which let one of the world's first civilizations grow there.

problems.q: What was the early Sumerian writing system called?
Fill in the blank: Cuneiform was made by pressing ______ into clay.
True or False: Sumerian math was based on the number 60, which is why we still have 60-minute hours.
Name two important 'firsts' the Sumerians gave the world.
problems.answer: Any two of: cuneiform writing, the first cities, the wheel, and math based on the number 60.

problems.q: Why were Sumerian inventions like writing and the wheel so important?
problems.answer: Because they shaped and were used by civilizations for thousands of years, helping people record information, build cities, and travel or move goods.

problems.q: Who was Hammurabi?
problems.answer: A Babylonian king who wrote down one of the first sets of laws.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Hammurabi's laws followed the idea of 'an eye for an ______.'
True or False: The Code of Hammurabi was carved on a tall stone for everyone to see.
What was the name of Hammurabi's famous set of laws?
Why was writing the laws down important for the people of Babylon?
problems.answer: Because written laws applied to everyone, so rules were the same for all instead of changing based on whatever a ruler felt like that day.

problems.q: What is monotheism?
problems.answer: The belief in just one God.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: The Israelites stressed following moral laws like the Ten ______.
True or False: Most of the Israelites' neighbors also believed in only one God.
Name the three religions that were later shaped by the idea of one God.
Why were the ancient Israelites considered different from most of their neighbors?
problems.answer: Because they believed in just one God (monotheism), while most of their neighbors worshipped many gods.

problems.q: Along which river did ancient Egypt grow?
Fill in the blank: Each year the Nile flooded and left behind rich ______ soil perfect for farming.
True or False: The desert around Egypt acted like a natural wall that protected it from invaders.
Which Greek historian called Egypt 'the gift of the Nile'?
Explain why Egypt was called 'the gift of the Nile.'
problems.answer: Because the Nile's yearly floods left rich soil for farming, making the river so important to Egypt's survival that Herodotus called Egypt a gift of the Nile.

problems.q: What were the Egyptian pyramids built to be?
Fill in the blank: The Egyptian picture-writing system was called ______.
True or False: The Egyptians invented papyrus, an early kind of paper.
Name two fields in which the Egyptians were skilled.
problems.answer: Any two of: medicine, math, and engineering.

problems.q: Why do many Egyptian achievements still amaze scientists today?
problems.answer: Because the Egyptians built enormous stone pyramids and made advances in medicine, math, and engineering that were remarkable for their time.

5-3.title: Pharaohs and Key Figures of Egypt

problems.q: What was a pharaoh?
problems.answer: A king of Egypt who was seen as a god-like leader.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: King ______'s untouched tomb was discovered in 1922.
True or False: Hatshepsut was one of the few female pharaohs of Egypt.
Name two things pharaohs organized.
problems.answer: Any two of: building projects, armies, and trade.

problems.q: Why were pharaohs so powerful in ancient Egypt?
problems.answer: Because they were seen as god-like leaders and they organized the kingdom's building projects, armies, and trade.

problems.q: In what river valley did one of the earliest civilizations grow?
problems.answer: The Indus River Valley (in what is now Pakistan and India).

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Two famous Indus Valley cities were Harappa and ______.
True or False: Indus Valley cities had indoor plumbing and sewer systems.
Name two advanced features of Indus Valley cities.
problems.answer: Any two of: brick houses, straight streets, indoor plumbing, and sewer systems.

problems.q: What does the careful planning of cities like Mohenjo-Daro tell us about this society?
problems.answer: It shows the society was very organized, with straight streets, brick houses, and planned plumbing and sewer systems.

6-2.title: Aryan Migrations and the Caste System

problems.q: Which group migrated into India after the Indus cities declined?
Fill in the blank: Society in India became divided into ranked groups called the ______ system.
True or False: In the caste system, people could easily move from one caste to another.
In the caste system, what decided a person's role in life?
problems.answer: The family (caste) they were born into.

problems.q: Explain how the caste system affected a person's life.
problems.answer: The caste a person was born into decided their role in life, and people generally could not move to a different caste, so their job and status were set from birth.

problems.q: Name two ideas that Hinduism teaches.
problems.answer: Any two of: karma, reincarnation, and many gods seen as forms of one spirit.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Buddhism began when a prince named Siddhartha Gautama, called the ______, taught his ideas.
True or False: Both Hinduism and Buddhism started in India.
According to the Buddha, what leads to peace?
Why are Hinduism and Buddhism both important to world history?
problems.answer: Because both began in India and spread across Asia, influencing the beliefs and cultures of many peoples.

problems.q: Who was the greatest ruler of the Mauryan Empire?
Fill in the blank: The Gupta Empire is often called India's '______ Age.'
True or False: Asoka spread Buddhism and ideas of peace after a terrible war.
Name two areas in which Gupta thinkers made advances.
problems.answer: Any two of: math, science, and art.

problems.q: Why is the Gupta Empire remembered as a 'Golden Age'?
problems.answer: Because of its great advances in math, science, and art, including helping create the number zero and our modern number symbols.

7-1.title: Rivers, Dynasties, and the Mandate of Heaven

problems.q: Along which two rivers did Chinese civilization grow?
Fill in the blank: A ruling family in ancient China was called a ______.
True or False: The Mandate of Heaven said a ruler could keep the right to rule even if he was cruel and unfair.
What was the Mandate of Heaven?
problems.answer: The idea that heaven gave a ruler the right to rule only as long as he ruled wisely and fairly.

problems.q: Explain what people believed would happen if a dynasty became cruel or weak.
problems.answer: They believed the dynasty had lost the Mandate of Heaven, so it could be replaced by a new ruler or dynasty.

problems.q: What did Confucius teach?
problems.answer: Respect, good manners, and that leaders should set a good example.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Laozi taught a way of life called Daoism, which is living simply and in harmony with ______.
True or False: Legalism, taught by Han Fei Zi, was the belief that strict laws and harsh punishments keep order.
Which thinker taught Daoism?
How were the ideas of Confucius and the Legalists different about how to keep order?
problems.answer: Confucius believed order came from respect, good manners, and leaders setting a good example, while Legalists believed order came from strict laws and harsh punishments.

problems.q: Name two things ancient China invented.
problems.answer: Any two of: paper, silk, the compass, and gunpowder.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: China built the Great ______ to defend their land.
True or False: The Silk Roads carried Chinese silk west and brought new goods and ideas back east.
What were the Silk Roads?
problems.answer: Long trade routes that connected China with other regions and carried goods and ideas.

problems.q: Why were the Silk Roads important to the ancient world?
problems.answer: Because they connected China, India, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean, letting goods and ideas spread between distant lands.

problems.q: Who led the Mongols in building their empire?
Fill in the blank: ______ Khan, Genghis Khan's grandson, ruled China and welcomed travelers like Marco Polo.
True or False: The Mongols built the largest connected land empire in history.
Which famous traveler visited Kublai Khan's China?
Explain how Mongol control helped trade and ideas spread.
problems.answer: Mongol control made the Silk Roads safer, so traders and travelers could move along them more easily, helping goods and ideas spread even farther.

8-1.title: City-States and the Birth of Democracy

problems.q: What was a Greek city-state called?
Fill in the blank: ______ created an early form of democracy where citizens could vote on laws.
True or False: In Athens, women, enslaved people, and foreigners were not allowed to vote.
What is a democracy?
problems.answer: A form of government in which citizens can vote on laws and take part in government.

problems.q: Why are Greek ideas about government still important today?
problems.answer: Because Greek ideas about voting and the rule of law influenced and continue to shape governments around the world.

problems.q: What did Athens value?
Fill in the blank: Sparta focused almost entirely on training tough ______ from a young age.
True or False: Athens and Sparta were very similar city-states with the same way of life.
Which city-state was famous for its strong, well-trained army?
Explain one major difference between Athens and Sparta.
problems.answer: Athens valued education, art, and democracy, while Sparta focused almost entirely on training tough soldiers, showing two very different ways of life.

problems.q: What did the Greek city-states do when the Persian Empire invaded?
problems.answer: They united and fought together, winning surprising victories.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: The Greeks won famous victories over Persia at battles like Marathon and ______.
True or False: In the Peloponnesian War, Athens and Sparta fought against each other.
Which war weakened Greece by turning Greek city-states against one another?
What do these two wars show about the Greek city-states?
problems.answer: They show the strength of Greek teamwork against Persia, but also the danger of fighting among themselves, which weakened Greece.

8-4.title: Greek Achievements and the Hellenistic Age

problems.q: Name two famous Greek philosophers.
problems.answer: Any two of: Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: ______ the Great conquered a huge empire and spread Greek culture across the Middle East and Asia.
True or False: The Greeks created the Olympics and early theater.
What is the name of the age that began when Greek culture spread across the Middle East and Asia?
Why was the Hellenistic Age important to the ancient world?
problems.answer: Because Alexander's conquests blended Greek culture with Eastern cultures, shaping the ancient world for centuries.

problems.q: What is a republic?
problems.answer: A government in which citizens elect leaders to make decisions for them.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: In the Roman Republic, citizens elected leaders called ______ to make decisions.
True or False: Roman ideas like separation of powers and the rule of law influenced later governments, including the United States.
What was the duty of Roman citizens to take part in their government called?
Why is the Roman Republic important to governments today?
problems.answer: Because its ideas of separation of powers, the rule of law, and electing leaders influenced later governments, including the United States.

9-2.title: The Punic Wars and Roman Expansion

problems.q: Which city did Rome fight in the Punic Wars?
Fill in the blank: There were ______ Punic Wars between Rome and Carthage.
True or False: Carthage's general Hannibal marched elephants over the mountains.
What did Rome do to Carthage at the end of the Punic Wars?
Why were the Punic Wars so important for Rome?
problems.answer: Because winning made Rome the master of the Mediterranean and set the stage for a mighty empire.

problems.q: Which Roman general took control before being assassinated?
Fill in the blank: ______ became the first emperor of Rome.
True or False: The long period of peace at the start of the Roman Empire was called the Pax Romana.
What happened to power in Rome as it changed from a republic to an empire?
problems.answer: Power shifted from elected leaders to one powerful emperor.

problems.q: Explain how Rome changed from a republic into an empire.
problems.answer: As the republic struggled, Julius Caesar took control and was assassinated, then his heir Augustus became the first emperor, shifting power to one ruler and beginning the Roman Empire.

problems.q: Name two things the Romans were famous for building.
problems.answer: Any two of: roads, aqueducts, concrete buildings, and laws.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Roman ______ carried water across long distances.
True or False: Christianity began in Roman lands and slowly spread until it became the empire's main religion.
What did early Christianity teach?
problems.answer: Belief in one God and in Jesus.

problems.q: How did Roman roads and trade help Christianity spread?
problems.answer: Roman roads and trade routes let people, goods, and ideas travel quickly, so the new Christian beliefs spread across the empire faster.

9-5.title: The Fall of the Western Roman Empire

problems.q: Which half of the Roman Empire slowly declined and fell?
problems.answer: The western half (the Western Roman Empire).

problems.q: Fill in the blank: By the year ______ AD the Western Roman Empire had fallen.
True or False: One cause of Rome's fall was that the empire was so huge it was hard to defend.
Name two causes of the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
problems.answer: Any two of: weak leaders, money problems, a huge size hard to defend, and invasions by outside groups.

problems.q: Why is the fall of the Western Roman Empire seen as the end of an era?
problems.answer: Because its fall in 476 AD ended the ancient classical world in Europe.

10-1.title: The Kingdoms of Kush and Axum

problems.q: Where was the kingdom of Kush located?
problems.answer: South of Egypt along the Nile River.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: The kingdom of Kush traded gold, ivory, and ______.
True or False: Axum was one of the first kingdoms to adopt Christianity.
What made the kingdom of Axum powerful?
problems.answer: It became a powerful trading center in East Africa.

problems.q: What do the kingdoms of Kush and Axum show us about ancient Africa?
problems.answer: They show that great civilizations grew across the whole continent of Africa, not only in Egypt.

10-2.title: Trade, Barter, and Money in the Ancient World

problems.q: What is barter?
problems.answer: Trading goods directly for other goods, like trading grain for cloth.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Over time, civilizations created money, such as ______, to make trading easier.
True or False: Money is used as a medium of exchange that makes trading easier.
Give an example of barter.
problems.answer: Trading grain for cloth (any direct swap of goods for goods).

problems.q: Why did using money make trade easier than barter?
problems.answer: With barter you had to find someone who wanted exactly what you had, but money works as a medium of exchange that everyone accepts, so trading is simpler.

problems.q: What does scarcity mean?
problems.answer: There is never enough of everything people want, so choices must be made about resources.

problems.q: Fill in the blank: Choosing one thing means giving up another, which is called ______ cost.
True or False: Because of scarcity, societies must make choices about how to use resources like land, labor, and tools.
Name two ways ancient civilizations dealt with scarcity.
Explain how opportunity cost works when a society makes an economic choice.
problems.answer: Because resources are scarce, choosing to use them for one thing means giving up the chance to use them for something else, and that given-up choice is the opportunity cost.
